derived_cause: The 58-item checklist is a transcription of a login-gated, owner-side platform tick-list, so nothing in the repository can be made to go red against it, and the summary counts are hand-composed rather than counted. Four independent links: (1) the source page is behind platform auth. The mirrored approval-guidelines submission page reads 'Login required / You must be logged in to view the approval guidelines' (docs/stake-engine-live/submission-checklist.md:22-24, fetched 2026-07-04, unchanged at the 2026-07-29 recapture docs/stake-engine-live/2026-07-29/approval_guidelines_submission_checklist.md:26-28), so the convention (d) docs-watch mirror, which fetches public pages headlessly, never captured the 58 items; the only copy in the repository is the owner's manual transcription (STAKE_GUIDELINES_SELF_ASSESSMENT.md:3-6). A requirement that exists only as transcribed prose gives a gate nothing to key on. (2) the tick-list itself is an owner action on the platform (:5-6 'the platform shows it as a manual tick-list at 0 of 58 ... ticking it there is the owner's action, not ours'), so 0/58 is not a repository-controllable state and no CI step could assert it. (3) the one gate that reads committed markdown, scripts/qa/doc_currency_gate.mjs, only checks CITATION liveness: DEAD_PATH, STALE_LINE, DEAD_SYMBOL, DEAD_COMMIT, DEAD_DOCREF plus opt-in <!--CHECK:--> predicates limited to exists/!exists/count/grep/!grep (doc_currency_gate.mjs:36-50). None of those can read a status word, a FAIL row or a count, and this file's four existing findings are frozen as accepted baseline debt (scripts/qa/doc_currency_baseline.json:459-480), so the document can carry an open FAIL with that gate green. (4) gate coverage of individual items is incidental and per-defect, never per-checklist: item 15 is defended by frontend/scripts/layout_fit_gate.mjs:5, item 25 by frontend/scripts/dist_hygiene_gate.mjs:286-290, item 46 by frontend/scripts/locale_launch_conformance.mjs:123, item 6 by frontend/scripts/dist_hygiene_gate.mjs:210-216, each arriving with its own fix ticket (TR-065, TR-066, TR-067) rather than from any enumeration of the 58 rows. Nothing maps rows to gates, so the remaining rows have no CI step, no test and no tracker row, exactly as the record observes. (5) the statuses are additionally not machine-countable: the document declares a strict five-value vocabulary (:13-21) but six of the 58 rows carry non-atomic statuses (19 'PASS in English', 23 and 24 'PASS with a defect', 32 'OWNER/OBSERVE', 34 'PASS in mechanism', 48 'PASS in code, OBSERVE live', plus 53's caveat), so no consistent partition of the rows exists. Recounted mechanically over the 58 table rows: exactly 31 read bare PASS, 10 bare OBSERVE, 5 bare OWNER (6 including 53), 3 FAIL, 1 CONFLICT, 1 N/A, 6 hybrid. The summary's OBSERVE 14 is reachable only as 10 bare plus rows 23, 24, 32 and 48; OWNER 8 is unreachable from any partition, the maximum being 7 (5 bare + 53 + 32). The printed table therefore totals 58 only by inflating OWNER by one and leaving rows 19 and 34 in no bucket, which is why the document itself records at :176 that three separate OWNER figures disagreed and none had been recounted.
citations: CLAUDE.md convention (d), docs watch: refresh the live Stake Engine docs pages into docs/stake-engine-live/
reasoning: Spec first: docs/stake-engine-live/ is the mirrored specification corpus, and the page that would carry the 58 items is auth-walled in both the 2026-07-04 and 2026-07-29 captures, which is why the checklist reaches the repository only as prose. The counting claim was computed rather than asserted: a script parsed all 58 table rows and tallied the status cell, giving 31 bare PASS, 10 OBSERVE, 5 OWNER, 3 FAIL, 1 CONFLICT, 1 N/A and 6 hybrid rows, which reproduces PASS 31 exactly and makes OWNER 8 unreachable. Gate coverage was established by reading checks.yml and each gate's own header rather than by trusting the document's evidence column.
